mustRecognize: The intended product is a long-lived multicenter cardiomyopathy imaging platform.
A common core protocol and data model must coexist with evolvable substudies/modules.
Modules may be added or stopped without rewriting the whole Project.
Versioning, supersession and cross-document propagation are central requirements.
mustPreserve: The distinction between common core, individual modules and current adopted versions.
Unresolved platform governance, module lifecycle and document-allocation choices.
Rejected, stopped and superseded module states.
The limitation that protected platform-trial content is not runtime-accessible or required.
mustConsider: Common versus module-specific populations, measurements, data and documents.
Human adoption, versioning, dependency and propagation rules.
Document commitment/detail boundaries across core and module artifacts.
mustNotInvent: Protected source content, a platform precedent or a mandatory documentary pattern.
A specific module, governance body, stopping criterion or versioning algorithm.
A final DMP, SAP, Imaging Charter or CRF requirement for every module.
mustNotDo: Treat this optional scenario as part of the mandatory primary gate.
Require runtime access to rights-restricted platform-trial content.
Let template or document projections define Project truth.
Impose one universal platform architecture where several are defensible.
acceptableAlternativeFamilies: Master-protocol, platform-protocol or modular umbrella candidates compatible with explicit version governance.
Different common/module boundaries justified by scientific and operational dependencies.
Alternative document families and propagation strategies preserving Project identity and supersession.
requiredOwnershipBoundaries: Study Design may propose modular structures but human adoption governs the Project.
DOC-002R and Knowledge provide contextual evidence, not mandatory architecture.
TMP/DOC project current adopted truth and cannot create it.
QRY remains free to select the next legitimate action.
requiredEvidenceBehavior: Only admitted current patterns and Project knowledge are used.
Rights/access limitations and metadata-only status remain explicit.
No protected or non-stored content is implied to be runtime-readable.
requiredHumanBoundaries: Human adoption of platform architecture, common/module boundaries and lifecycle governance.
Human adoption of versioning and document-propagation strategy.
Human scientific judgment where modularity tradeoffs are context-dependent.
documentaryExpectations: Current core and module documents bind to the correct Project versions.
Stopped or superseded modules do not silently remain current.
Cross-document propagation is explicit without requiring all final specialized artifacts.
blockingFailureConditions: Project/module identity, version or supersession is materially lost.
Protected content, governance decisions or module facts are invented.
The first divergence cannot be reconstructed.
nonBlockingFindingExamples: Optional platform content is not runtime-indexed.
A secondary modular architecture is omitted.
